main_text.p: vivitur, pervenirent: deinceps jam securi[?] nunquam se ab illo esse casuros. Quæ præsum-tio, in isto tentationum loco, non expedit: ubi tanta est infirmitas, ut superbiam possit gene-rare securitas.&c.

Non nego tamen hæc, & similia Augustini loca, simpliciter, ut olim, ita hodie à Pōtificiis solere accipi, pro incertitudine scientiæ nostræ, quòd simus in fide, aut prædestinati; contra expressum præceptum Apostoli, 2 Cor.13. v.5: Vos-met-ipsos tentate, an sitis in fide: vos ipsos proba-te. An non agnoscitis vosmet ipsos; videli-cet Jesum Christum in vobis esse? Nisi forte re-probi estis.&c. Olim ita accepisse videtur Prosper.Prosper, in hisce duriffimis, lib.2. de vo-cat.Gent.cap.28. Qui ad obædiendum sibi, ipsum velle sic donat; ut etiam a perseveratu-ris illam mutabilitatem, quæ poteft nolle, non auferat: alioqui nemo unquam fidelium recessis-set à fide. Verum & hoc ex contextu ipso mollescit. Neque enim aliud docet; quam, manere in regeneratis, Dei virtute perseveraturis, perpetuam carnis & spiritus luctâ, infirmitatem, im-per-

page.notes: The printed text ends mid-word with "per-" at the foot of the page, and continues on the next page. The opening passage is a fragment continuing from the previous page. The line-end at "securi[?]" is doubtful: the word may be securitas, with the end cut off. "Pōtificiis" is written with an abbreviation stroke over the o (printed Pötificiis). The quotation marks in the left margin beside the top lines are not transcribed as text. The right edge shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.
